Schlosser, F., Jesper, M., Vogelsang, J., Walmsley, T.G., Arpagaus, C. and Hesselbach, J. (2020). Large-scale heat pumps: Applications, performance, economic feasibility and industrial integration. Renewable and Sustainable Energy Reviews, 133, 110219. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.rser.2020.110219

Locators are printed article page numbers (page 1 = PDF page 1). A review of electric-driven large-scale heat pumps: it classifies 155 case studies, builds COP regression models from manufacturer data and economic nomograms. Loaded as heat-pump_industrial: technology limits per heat pump type (capacity, sink temperature ranges of validity), the COP at each integration case printed in Table 5 (modelled COP at the case lift, stored as % = COP x 100), the investment reference of 420 EUR/kWth (Table 4) and 400 EUR/kWth (worked example), and the levelized cost of heat per case (Table 6, converted ct/kWh to EUR/MWh). Not loaded: regression parameters (Tables 1-3, in other-values; a main-file formula cannot hold them), nomogram curves, break-even price ratios, GHG abatement cost curves (figures only, values read from charts are not in the main file), case-study COPs that are only plotted (Fig. 5). Overlap: arpagaus_2018_001 and iea-hpt_2023_001 already hold product-level capacity, temperature and COP for commercial HTHPs; this paper adds the modelled integration COPs, the investment reference and the levelized costs, and shares only the 0.4-0.6 second-law efficiency range (other-values).
